verdict.justification: Both deliverables follow the prompt's instructions accurately, hitting every required slide topic, date, and title. However, Deliverable A is significantly more thorough and insightful as a project management deliverable. On Slide 4 (Progress Summary), Deliverable A extracts and summarizes the non-financial resource usage table (days used per role vs. planned) from INPUT 2, which explains the root cause of the Month 1 overspend (front-loaded Information Manager days), whereas Deliverable B omits the resource effort breakdown completely. On Slide 5 (Project Spend), Deliverable A provides a full line-item breakdown of all cost categories against their budgets, while Deliverable B groups Materials and Travel & Expenses into summary rows. Furthermore, Deliverable A proactively spots a timeline conflict in the Project Log (Output 1 V2.0 being sent to the assessor on 7 Nov before stakeholder comments are incorporated on 9 Nov) and raises it as a concrete decision point for the auditor on Slide 8. Finally, Deliverable B has a minor chronological lapse on Slide 7 where it refers to a November 3rd review in the past tense despite the report being dated October 30th.
